title: Over an algebraically closed field, few differentials at a closed point imply smoothness there
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $\mathfrak m\subset S$ a maximal ideal, with localization $S_{\mathfrak m}$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=S_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak mS_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\Omega_{S/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})$ the Krull dimension of the ring $S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. If $$\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak m)}\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak m)\le\dim(S_{\mathfrak m}),$$ then $k\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]: there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak m$ such that the localization $S_g$ of $S$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$ is a smooth $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TS (lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar, line 38505), implication (2) => (4); proof lines 38524-38604 ((2) => (1) by Lemma 00TR lemma-rank-omega, then (1) => (4) by the presentation argument with Lemmas 00SC lemma-lci, 00T7, 00TE); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (00TS,algebra-lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar)

proof.text: Put $R=S_{\mathfrak m}$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mR$ and $\kappa=R/\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The field $\kappa$ is a finite type $k$-algebra: it is $S/\mathfrak m$, generated by the images of the finite algebra generators of $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] it is finite over $k$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-alg-closed-finite-extension-trivial] the structure map $k\to\kappa$ is an isomorphism. In particular $\kappa/k$ is finitely generated and separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], and $\Omega_{\kappa/k}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The field $k$ is Noetherian, $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $R$ is Noetherian local by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TR (lemma-rank-omega, lines 38475-38500), proof: residue field equals k by Theorem Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz); Lemma Tag 00TS (lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar), proof line 38525

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] to $k\to R\to\kappa=R/\mathfrak n$: there is an exact sequence $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\xrightarrow{\delta}\kappa\otimes_R\Omega_{R/k}\to\Omega_{\kappa/k}\to0$, where $\delta(a\bmod\mathfrak n^2)=1\otimes\mathrm da$. The map $\delta$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-residue-cotangent-injective], since the Noetherian local ring $R$ has finitely generated separable residue field $\kappa=k$ (step 1). The last term vanishes by step 1, so $\delta$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{R/k}\cong(\Omega_{S/k})_{\mathfrak m}$; tensoring with $\kappa$ identifies its fibre with $\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa$. Consequently $e:=\dim_\kappa(\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2)=\dim_\kappa(\Omega_{S/k}\otimes_S\kappa)\le d:=\dim R$, the hypothesis.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TR (lemma-rank-omega, lines 38475-38500), proof using Lemmas Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq) and 02HP (lemma-differential-seq-split); Tag 00TS, proof line 38525

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $d=\dim R\le e$ for the Noetherian local ring $R$ of step 1, and equality holds exactly when $R$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Step 2 gives $e\le d$, hence $e=d$ and $R=S_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular local. This proves the source's equivalence of conditions (2) and (1), including the case $d=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TS (lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar), proof line 38525: (1), (2), (3) equivalent by Tag 00TR and the definition of a regular local ring

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $S=P/I$ with $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; let $\mathfrak M\subset P$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak m$. It is maximal since $P/\mathfrak M\cong S/\mathfrak m=\kappa$ is a field. The localization $A=P_{\mathfrak M}$ is regular local [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] of dimension $n$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], $A/IA\cong S_{\mathfrak m}=R$, which is regular local by step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters] to $A$ and $IA$: there are parameters $u_1,\dots,u_n$ generating its maximal ideal and $0\le c\le n$ with $IA=(u_1,\dots,u_c)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], these $c$ parameters form a regular sequence in $A$ and $A/IA$ is regular local of dimension $n-c$. Since $A/IA\cong R$ has dimension $d$, $c=n-d$. Thus the kernel of the localized presentation is generated by a regular sequence of exactly the codimension length.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TS (lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar), proof lines 38542-38585: polynomial presentation, regular local quotient and its n-d local equations; Lemma Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular), and Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM)

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-lci-regular-sequence-global-complete-intersection] now hold for $P$, $I$, $S$, $\mathfrak m$ and its inverse-image prime $\mathfrak M$: step 4 supplies the regular sequence generating $IP_{\mathfrak M}$. It gives $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak m$ such that $T=S_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Since $g\notin\mathfrak m$, $T$ is nonzero and $\mathfrak m_g=\mathfrak mT$ is a maximal ideal with $T_{\mathfrak m_g}\cong S_{\mathfrak m}=R$. By the global complete intersection definition, choose $N,C\ge0$ and a $k$-algebra isomorphism $T\cong k[y_1,\dots,y_N]/(f_1,\dots,f_C)$ with $\dim T=N-C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-global-complete-intersection-equidimensional] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring], $N-C=\dim(T_{\mathfrak m_g})=d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TS (lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar), proof lines 38573-38593: shrink to a global complete intersection via Tag 00SC (lemma-lci), and its dimension n-c

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] and the identification $\kappa(\mathfrak m_g)=\kappa(\mathfrak m)$, the fibre of $\Omega_{T/k}$ at $\mathfrak m_g$ has dimension $e=d=N-C$ (steps 2, 3 and 5). In the presentation of step 5 put $Q=k[y_1,\dots,y_N]$, $J=(f_1,\dots,f_C)$ and identify $T=Q/J$. The global complete intersection over the field is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection]. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-conormal-free], $J/J^2$ is free on the $C$ classes of the $f_j$; by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], $T\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/k}$ is free on $\mathrm dy_1,\dots,\mathrm dy_N$. In the conormal sequence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps], $J/J^2\to T\otimes_Q\Omega_{Q/k}\to\Omega_{T/k}\to0$, the first map sends the class of $f_j$ to $\sum_i(\partial f_j/\partial y_i)\mathrm dy_i$. Tensoring its right-exact tail with $\kappa(\mathfrak m_g)$ gives a cokernel of dimension $N-C$ for an $N\times C$ Jacobian matrix over that field. Therefore the matrix has rank $C$; some $C\times C$ minor has nonzero image in $\kappa(\mathfrak m_g)$, hence its image in $T$ lies outside $\mathfrak m_g$. (For $C=0$, the unique empty minor is $1$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TS (lemma-characterize-smooth-kbar), proof lines 38595-38605: naive cotangent matrix has rank c by Tag 00TR; the conormal sequence is Tag 00RU and polynomial differentials Tag 00RX

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-smooth-jacobian] to the presentation of $T$ and the prime $\mathfrak m_g$: the maximal minor outside $\mathfrak m_g$ from step 6 implies that $k\to T$ is smooth at $\mathfrak m_g$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Thus there is $h\in T\setminus\mathfrak m_g$ with $T_h$ smooth over $k$. Write $h=a/g^r$ for some $a\in S$ and $r\ge0$; $a\notin\mathfrak m$, and $T_h\cong S_{ga}$, since inverting $h$ after inverting $g$ is the same as inverting $a$ and $g$. The element $ga\notin\mathfrak m$ and $S_{ga}$ is smooth over $k$, exactly the smoothness of $k\to S$ at $\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

split_report.summary: Seven-step split of Algebra 00TS (2) => (4): 00TR via the existing exact-conormal and separable-residue nodes gives cotangent dimension equal to the differential fibre; the bound makes S_m regular. Present S as k[x]/I; regular quotient parameters (00NR) and regular-sequence dimension drop (00NQ) give local equations, and 00SC shrinks to a global complete intersection. Its conormal sequence and the bound force the Jacobian matrix to have full column rank at m, so 00TE gives smoothness. Existing DAG nodes cover each cited result; no new nodes. The source and tags 00TR, 00TS, 00NR, 00NQ, 00SC, 00RU, 00RX and 00TE were checked in algebra.tex and tags/tags. Tested d=0, c=0 and S=0 (the maximal ideal excludes S=0).
